what_it_does: Name-value pair (NVP) stores are databases that map a name (a string label) to a value, used heavily in caching systems, configuration management, and data analytics. Looking up a name requires reading candidate entries and checking whether their name field matches the query. Today this check happens on the host CPU, which means all the raw data must travel from the SSD (solid-state storage) over a bus to the CPU just to be filtered — wasting bandwidth for the many entries that do not match. ANVIL embeds the name-matching logic inside the SSD itself, so only matching entries leave the drive. Unlike prior work that handled only one data format, ANVIL is designed to support a broad range of NVP encodings (arrays, dictionaries, key-value stores, and data-mining structures) through a unified in-storage computation architecture.
